notes: Train, validation and test Parquet files are publicly listed. The compilation license explicitly preserves each image’s original source terms and grants no extra rights to those images. The card exposes a platform column without listing its values, so operating-system coverage remains unspecified.

dataset_profile.notes: Card-reported row counts and unique-screen counts are different units. The source field is important for the per-image license terms; the compilation does not relicense original images.

value.declared: Wave UI Dataset License; per-image source terms retained
value.basis: Publisher compilation license; individual images keep their source-dataset terms and receive no additional rights from this compilation.

data.reason: The compilation expressly does not relicense its images and lists differing source terms. No blanket permissive data license is appropriate.

name: WebPRM checklist-generation data
summary: Web-task context, starting observations and action history paired with structured checklists and subgoal analyses for checklist generation.
notes: Five public Parquet shards are present. This collection provides checklist-generation supervision and is distinct from the previously cataloged chosen/rejected preference data. The Hub calls its split test; that label is preserved. No data license is declared.

dataset_profile.notes: This is the checklist-generation release. No unique-task count or data permission is inferred.

name: UI-Genie reward data
summary: Mobile GUI reward annotations released for training UI-Genie’s trajectory-assessment model.
notes: The public manifest contains reward_data.jsonl but no separately packaged image archive. The card declares MIT. The 517k identifier is a release name; verified sample count and complete image packaging remain unspecified.

dataset_profile.notes: The public manifest contains reward_data.jsonl but no separately packaged image archive. The card declares MIT. The 517k identifier is a release name; verified sample count and complete image packaging remain unspecified.

name: UI-Genie trajectory data
summary: Synthetic mobile GUI trajectory supervision and screenshots released with the UI-Genie agent-training pipeline.
notes: Public JSONL annotations and screenshots are present. MIT is declared in the dataset card. The release name, model-card links and annotation filename use different size labels.

dataset_profile.notes: Public JSONL annotations and screenshots are present. MIT is declared in the dataset card. The release name, model-card links and annotation filename use different size labels.

name: OS-Genesis mobile training data
summary: Reverse-task-synthesis mobile trajectories released in separate AndroidControl and AndroidWorld training annotation files.
notes: The public manifest contains AC/AW JSONL training annotations and a screenshot archive. MIT is declared for the data in its own card, separately from Apache-2.0 declarations on some model checkpoints. The gated web-data release is a separate asset.

dataset_profile.notes: AC and AW refer to distinct target training sets; no sample count is inferred from the two JSONL files or ZIP packaging.

name: Holo2 4B
summary: A Qwen3-VL-based checkpoint for navigation and multi-step GUI actions across web, desktop and mobile interfaces.
notes: Two public safetensors shards are present and this 4B model card declares Apache-2.0. The same card assigns different terms to the 30B family member, so the 4B declaration is not generalized to the family.

name: Holo3 35B-A3B
summary: A sparse Qwen3.5-based GUI-action checkpoint released for navigation and computer-use workflows.
notes: Fourteen public safetensors shards are present. The card declares Apache-2.0 for this release and describes a 35B-total/3B-active MoE architecture. No unpublished enterprise benchmark or training corpus is added solely from its performance claims.

name: MAI-UI 8B
summary: A released MAI-UI checkpoint combining mobile GUI actions, agent-user interaction and tool-use-oriented navigation.
notes: Four public safetensors shards are present and Apache-2.0 is declared. The card presents family-wide results and device-cloud architecture.

name: ScienceBoard VMware environment
summary: A prebuilt Ubuntu virtual-machine archive containing the software environment used for ScienceBoard scientific computer-use tasks.
notes: The public Hub manifest contains VM.zip. This is an environment image hosted in a Hub model namespace. The card declares MIT metadata for the hosted release, but that does not relicense Ubuntu or included applications. VMware’s own terms apply separately.

weights.reason: This resource is a prebuilt Ubuntu VMware environment archive (VM.zip). MIT Hub metadata in a model namespace cannot establish a weights license or relicense the guest OS and bundled applications.

name: ScienceBoard evaluation trajectories
summary: Archives of ScienceBoard agent evaluation runs, separated by agent configuration and screenshot, accessibility-tree or set-of-marks observation mode.
notes: The manifest exposes six ZIP archives but no README card or data-license declaration. The official project announces evaluation-result trajectories.

dataset_profile.notes: Observation modes follow publisher archive labels. No count or training-use permission is inferred.

name: UI-S1 released training examples
summary: A public example subset of the UI-S1 mobile training data, packaged as JSONL annotations and Parquet images.
notes: The release contains train_1000.jsonl and images.parquet. The official README explicitly describes 1,000 released examples and calls the release only part of the training dataset. Apache-2.0 is declared by the dataset card. The release contains part of the training corpus.

dataset_profile.notes: The count is explicitly reported by the publisher. Full training data remains outside this release.

name: ScreenSpot-v2 instruction variants
summary: Instruction variants over ScreenSpot-v2 screenshots that distinguish original commands, explicit actions, target descriptions and impossible operations.
notes: Public image files and desktop/mobile/web annotation JSON files are listed. This is a changed instruction set over an existing screenshot collection. No data license or precise example count is declared in the card; no paper relationship is inferred from its generic project/PDF links.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Publisher supplies original, action, description and negative instruction types; no common end-to-end success metric is asserted.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Reuses ScreenSpot-v2 imagery. Image-file counts, independent screenshots and tasks are different units.

name: Holo4 35B-A3B BF16
summary: A Qwen3.6-based computer-use checkpoint designed to request GUI actions, code execution and tool calls through an external agent harness.
notes: The public manifest contains 26 safetensors shards for the BF16 checkpoint and the card declares Apache-2.0. Quantized FP8/NVFP4/GGUF variants belong to the same model release. The card also contains demos and scores for Holo4-27B. No training corpus or runtime was downloaded.

name: MAI-UI inference and evaluation code
summary: Published MAI-UI grounding and navigation-agent implementations with inference demos and evaluation scripts.
notes: The original implementation is in the MAI-UI/ subdirectory, with an Apache-2.0 LICENSE there. The current root README also promotes Qwen-UI-Agent, but that follow-up directory contains only documentation/display assets in the inspected tree. The original MAI-UI/ implementation is released; the follow-up Qwen-UI-Agent directory contains documentation/display assets in the inspected tree.

value.basis: Retained MAI-UI/LICENSE and MAI-UI README; applies to the inspected implementation, subject to third-party components.

code.reason: The implementation and LICENSE live under MAI-UI/. The Apache-2.0 declaration is scoped to MAI-UI/ implementation and LICENSE.

name: Mobile-Bench-v2 released data
summary: Offline mobile-agent task data spanning common tasks and released noisy, contaminated and ambiguous-instruction subsets.
notes: The card distinguishes complete common-simple/common-complex JSON files from sampled noisy and ambiguous subsets; common tasks also require the separately cataloged Mobile3M dataset. Card metadata says Apache-2.0, while the prose explicitly assigns Apache-2.0 to code and CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 to data. Do not apply the permissive header to dataset payloads, and do not describe every announced split as fully released.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Paper defines multi-path and noise/ambiguity evaluations; the public card identifies which files are full common-task sets and which are samples.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Release completeness differs by split. No full-benchmark sample total is inferred from the archive manifest.

data.reason: The same first-party card has an Apache-2.0 metadata header but explicitly assigns Apache-2.0 to code and CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 to the dataset in its License section. Preserve both declarations and leave a single data license unresolved instead of displaying the permissive header as the data permission.

name: End-to-End Goal-Driven Web Navigation
summary: Introduces WebNav for converting websites into goal-directed hyperlink navigation tasks and WikiNav for evaluating language-conditioned navigation and question answering on Wikipedia.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Interactive Task and Concept Learning from Natural Language Instructions and GUI Demonstrations
summary: Introduces PUMICE, an agent that learns mobile-app procedures and conditional concepts through natural-language conversation and GUI demonstrations, recursively resolving ambiguous instructions with users.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: ActionBert: Leveraging User Actions for Semantic Understanding of User Interfaces
summary: Pretrains ActionBert on user interaction traces to combine visual, linguistic, and UI-structure features. It evaluates the resulting UI representations on tasks including icon classification and description-based component retrieval.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Understanding Mobile GUI: from Pixel-Words to Screen-Sentences
summary: Models mobile screens as atomic text and graphic components whose relationships are learned by a Screen Transformer. The work introduces RICO-PW annotations and evaluates metadata-free screen understanding on relation, clickability, retrieval, and app-classification tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Learning to Denoise Raw Mobile UI Layouts for Improving Datasets at Scale
summary: Introduces CLAY, a pipeline that repairs noisy mobile UI layouts by removing nodes without valid visual counterparts and assigning semantic element types, supported by human-annotated layouts for evaluation.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Enabling Conversational Interaction with Mobile UI using Large Language Models
summary: Studies few-shot prompting of a single language model for four mobile-UI interaction tasks, aiming to support conversational interface use without a separate trained model for each task.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Spotlight: Mobile UI Understanding using Vision-Language Models with a Focus
summary: Introduces Spotlight, a vision-language model conditioned on a UI screenshot and a selected region of interest. It evaluates screenshot-based mobile UI understanding and explores multitask learning and few-shot prompting.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Towards Better Semantic Understanding of Mobile Interfaces
summary: Augments RICO screens and view hierarchies with human labels for icon shape and meaning and for links between UI elements and text labels. It compares image-only and multimodal models on semantic understanding of previously unseen apps.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Lexi: Self-Supervised Learning of the UI Language
summary: Introduces Lexi and UICaption to learn UI image-text representations from descriptions of interface functionality. Evaluation covers UI action entailment, instruction-based retrieval, referring-expression grounding, and UI entity recognition.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
summary: Introduces recursive criticism and improvement prompting for language-model agents performing computer tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ with a small number of demonstrations per task.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models
summary: Trains WebGUM offline from demonstrations by jointly tuning an instruction-following language model and a vision encoder over webpage screenshots and HTML. The agent predicts browser actions and is evaluated on MiniWoB, WebShop, and Mind2Web.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Hierarchical Prompting Assists Large Language Model on Web Navigation
summary: Separates web navigation prompting into a SUMMARIZER that extracts action-relevant observations and an ACTOR that chooses the next action from the condensed context.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
summary: Studies instruction-following agents that observe screenshots and act through a generic mouse-and-keyboard action space, evaluating pixel-based pretraining for GUI tasks on MiniWoB++.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
summary: Introduces InstructExcel, a benchmark for generating Excel OfficeScripts from natural-language requests, built using scripts recorded from user actions and a collection of existing spreadsheets.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. This is an application-specific automation benchmark grounded in recorded Excel user actions. Its execution interface is OfficeScripts, making it adjacent to visual GUI navigation benchmarks.

name: Explore, Select, Derive, and Recall: Augmenting LLM with Human-like Memory for Mobile Task Automation
summary: Introduces MobileGPT, which organizes mobile-app experience into reusable subtasks using an explore, select, derive, and recall cycle. Its memory supports learning task procedures and adapting them to new contexts.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
summary: Introduces AgentBoard, a multiturn agent evaluation framework with intermediate progress metrics and analysis tools. Its broader task suite includes WebShop and WebArena interactions with stepwise progress measurements.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. The full paper documents search/click WebShop actions and 11 browser actions in WebArena, while the overall benchmark also covers non-web domains.

name: GPTVoiceTasker: Advancing Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency Through Dynamic Interface Exploration and Learning
summary: Introduces GPTVoiceTasker, a mobile assistant that interprets user commands, executes device interactions, and learns from prior commands to streamline later task execution. The work includes a user study of task efficiency.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WIPI: A New Web Threat for LLM-Driven Web Agents
summary: Studies WIPI, a black-box indirect-instruction threat in which webpage content redirects LLM-driven web agents. Evaluation spans plugin-based agents, Web GPTs, and open-source web-agent implementations.
verify_terms: WIPI: A New Web Threat f
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: PPTC-R benchmark: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models for PowerPoint Task Completion
summary: Benchmarks robustness of API-based PowerPoint completion under sentence-level, semantic, and multilingual instruction perturbations and changes to the available API set.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. The benchmark directly concerns PowerPoint task automation but executes through APIs, so it remains adjacent.

name: Enhancing Mobile "How-to" Queries with Automated Search Results Verification and Reranking
summary: Executes instructions from mobile how-to search results inside a controlled Android environment, then uses the observed success of those instructions to verify and rerank technical-support results.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Grounded Language Agent for Product Search via Intelligent Web Interactions
summary: Introduces GLAINTEL, a Flan-T5-based product-search web agent studied under unsupervised learning, demonstration-based training, and unsupervised domain adaptation. It compares ways to combine demonstrations with reinforcement learning.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Navigating WebAI: Training Agents to Complete Web Tasks with Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement learning for MiniWoB web tasks and investigates whether agents understand HTML structure or memorize target elements.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Unveiling Disparities in Web Task Handling Between Human and Web Agent
summary: Compares human think-aloud web-task behavior with web-agent planning, action, and reflection. The analysis highlights differences in updating plans, handling ambiguity, and investigating failures.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: V-Zen: Efficient GUI Understanding and Precise Grounding With A Novel Multimodal LLM
summary: Describes V-Zen, a multimodal GUI model with dual-resolution image encoders for grounding and next-action prediction, fine-tuned using GUIDE interface elements and task sequences.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The related GUIDE dataset paper remains a separate record; this annotation describes the V-Zen model contribution.

name: WONDERBREAD: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Foundation Models on Business Process Management Tasks
summary: Introduces WONDERBREAD, a benchmark pairing human WebArena workflow demonstrations with screen recordings, action logs, and written procedures. Six evaluation tasks cover documentation, knowledge transfer, and process improvement beyond end-to-end execution.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The demonstrations were rehearsed; their completion rate measures rehearsed human performance.

name: MobileExperts: A Dynamic Tool-Enabled Agent Team in Mobile Devices
summary: Introduces MobileExperts, which assembles mobile-agent teams, lets agents explore and formulate tools, and coordinates them through two levels of planning. A benchmark organizes tasks by hierarchical intelligence levels.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: EIA: Environmental Injection Attack on Generalist Web Agents for Privacy Leakage
summary: Evaluates privacy-directed webpage instruction injection against generalist web agents using PII-related interaction steps from Mind2Web, including attempts to expose specific user information or entire requests.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Steward: Natural Language Web Automation
summary: Introduces Steward, a natural-language browser automation system that repeatedly plans and executes website actions. The paper examines completion detection, state representation, responsiveness, and caching in real-site tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AXIS: Efficient Human-Agent-Computer Interaction with API-First LLM-Based Agents
summary: Introduces AXIS, an API-first application agent that can use UI actions and expand its available APIs through automated application exploration. The work evaluates the approach on Microsoft Word tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Harnessing Webpage UIs for Text-Rich Visual Understanding
summary: Builds MultiUI by generating instructions from webpage accessibility trees and pairing them with screenshots for multimodal training. Evaluation examines web-interface understanding, including VisualWebBench and Mind2Web, and transfer to other text-rich visual tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Beyond Browsing: API-Based Web Agents
summary: Compares browsing-only, API-only, and hybrid web agents on WebArena, examining how access to application APIs changes task execution alongside browser interaction.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: From Context to Action: Analysis of the Impact of State Representation and Context on the Generalization of Multi-Turn Web Navigation Agents
summary: Analyzes how interaction history and webpage representation affect multiturn web-agent generalization across unfamiliar websites, task categories, and geographic settings.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Foundations and Recent Trends in Multimodal Mobile Agents: A Survey
summary: Surveys multimodal mobile agents, organizing prompt-based and training-based approaches alongside evaluation benchmarks, supporting technologies, and open challenges in mobile task execution.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: From Novice to Expert: LLM Agent Policy Optimization via Step-wise Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces StepAgent, which compares agent and expert actions to supply intermediate rewards for policy learning, with implicit-reward and inverse-RL variants. Evaluation includes WebShop and Mind2Web alongside non-web tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. Official full-paper experimental sections explicitly evaluate WebShop and Mind2Web; the overall optimization method also covers embodied and question-answering tasks.

name: The Dawn of GUI Agent: A Preliminary Case Study with Claude 3.5 Computer Use
summary: Presents a preliminary study of Claude 3.5 Computer Use across desktop tasks and software, analyzing planning, action, and critique behavior and providing a framework for deploying GUI-automation models.
verify_terms: The Dawn of GUI Agent: A
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Large Action Models: From Inception to Implementation
summary: Uses a Windows-agent case study to describe a development workflow for large action models, covering data collection, training, grounding, environment integration, and evaluation.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

summary: This study compares matched reasoning and non-reasoning vision-language models on static mobile GUI tasks and interactive AndroidWorld navigation. It finds that chain-of-thought effects vary across tasks and model families.
name: Does Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Help Mobile GUI Agent? An Empirical Study
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WebEvolver trains a co-evolving world model to predict web observations and generate additional agent-training trajectories. The same model supports look-ahead action selection at inference, with evaluation on live web-task benchmarks.
name: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GEM detects instructions outside a GUI agent’s capabilities by modeling distances in its input-embedding space with a Gaussian mixture. Experiments across mobile, computer and browser data also examine selective escalation to a cloud model when an input is detected as unfamiliar.
name: GEM: Gaussian Embedding Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Detection in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WebCoT turns reflection, look-ahead, branching and rollback procedures into chain-of-thought training rationales. Fine-tuning on these reconstructed trajectories is evaluated for web-agent self-improvement and transfer across navigation tasks.
name: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Uses an LLM judge to evaluate and filter synthetic GUI interaction trajectories for training a compact vision-language agent. OSWorld experiments assess the policy designed for local execution.
name: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: AgentSynth composes easily generated subtasks into longer computer-use tasks and trajectories with adjustable difficulty. Its evaluation uses the number of subtasks to probe how agent success changes as task complexity grows.
name: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.
name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Web-CogReasoner separates factual and conceptual web knowledge from procedural reasoning, using a structured curriculum to train a multimodal agent. Web-CogDataset and Web-CogBench support study of these capabilities alongside web-navigation evaluation.
name: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MVISU-Bench evaluates bilingual mobile tasks involving cross-app work, vague requests, user interaction and unethical instructions alongside ordinary single-app tasks. Its Aider prompting module is designed to clarify intent and mitigate risky execution within agent workflows.
name: MVISU-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents for Real-World Tasks by Multi-App, Vague, Interactive, Single-App and Unethical Instructions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: InquireMobile trains mobile agents to seek human confirmation at critical decisions using staged reinforcement fine-tuning and pre-action reasoning. InquireBench evaluates safe interaction and proactive inquiry, distinguishing asking for help from completing the underlying task.
name: InquireMobile: Teaching VLM-based Mobile Agent to Request Human Assistance via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.
name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MobileRAG combines retrieval and memory components to support mobile tasks that need external knowledge or long action sequences. MobileRAG-Eval is introduced to study these requirements on complex real-world app tasks.
name: MobileRAG: Enhancing Mobile Agent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.
name: BTL-UI: Blink-Think-Link Reasoning Model for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.
name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ProRe evaluates GUI task outcomes by having a reasoner assign targeted environment-probing tasks to specialist actors. The additional observations support reward judgments, with separate evaluation of judge accuracy and downstream agent task success.
name: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner-Actor Collaboration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.
name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.
name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GMS pairs a general vision-language scanner that proposes interface regions with a specialist locator that predicts coordinates within them. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine search coordinates the two components for GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.
name: Generalist Scanner Meets Specialist Locator: A Synergistic Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Robust GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.
name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.
name: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.
name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.
name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.
name: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.
name: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.
name: \textsc{GUI-Spotlight}: Adaptive Iterative Focus Refinement for Enhanced GUI Visual Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.
name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.
name: R-WoM: Retrieval-augmented World Model For Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ColorBench represents mobile tasks as graphs of states collected from real devices, providing a quasi-dynamic environment with multiple valid paths and error paths. It evaluates single-app and cross-app tasks using completion, subtask progress, and atomic diagnostics.
name: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.
name: Surfer 2: The Next Generation of Cross-Platform Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.
name: OpenPhone: Mobile Agentic Foundation Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.
name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.
name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.
name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.
name: ProBench: Benchmarking GUI Agents with Accurate Process Information
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.
name: Co-EPG: A Framework for Co-Evolution of Planning and Grounding in Autonomous GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.
name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: D-GARA evaluates Android GUI agents under runtime anomalies such as permission dialogs, battery warnings, and update prompts. Its modular environment embeds these interruptions in Android applications to study recovery and robustness.
name: D-GARA: A Dynamic Benchmarking Framework for GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: This study tests vision-language models as task-completion judges using screenshots and instructions from 42 built-in macOS applications. It evaluates judgment accuracy on human-labeled tasks and separately studies how judge feedback affects agent task success.
name: "Are We Done Yet?": A Vision-Based Judge for Autonomous Task Completion of Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: This work trains high-level schedulers with staged reinforcement learning driven by execution feedback. Its CES framework separates a Coordinator for planning and decomposition, a StateTracker for compressed context, and a low-level Executor.
name: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MPR-GUI evaluates GUI perception and reasoning through strictly aligned tasks in six languages. GUI-XLI adjusts non-English hidden representations toward English representations at language-sensitive layers during inference to address the measured cross-language gaps.
name: MPR-GUI: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multilingual Perception and Reasoning in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.
name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.
name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.
name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.
name: MVP: Multiple View Prediction Improves GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.
name: Step-GUI Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.
name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.
name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: DAVE trains a vision encoder for document images and web agents using self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised parsing and localization. It combines decoder-specific encoder merging with feature fusion and evaluates web localization and agent benchmarks alongside document tasks.
name: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.
name: EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.
name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

name: Ringer: Web Automation by Demonstration
summary: Introduces Ringer, which converts demonstrated webpage interactions into scripts combining actions, target selectors, and waiting conditions. It evaluates replay robustness on tasks recorded from real websites.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. The original manuscript and MSR BibTeX print Sarah Chasins and Ras Bodik. The official conference profiles expand these to Sarah E. Chasins and Rastislav Bodík; the printed publication names are preserved.

name: SUGILITE: Creating Multimodal Smartphone Automation by Demonstration
summary: Introduces SUGILITE, which combines spoken instructions, demonstrated Android actions, and UI hierarchies to generate reusable automation scripts. Its interface includes context checking and repairs for unfamiliar situations and changing app interfaces.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. Related to later APPINITE and PUMICE work but distinguished here by its 2017 three-author publication and base demonstration-automation contribution.

name: World of Bits: An Open-Domain Platform for Web-Based Agents
summary: Introduces World of Bits, a web-task platform combining human demonstrations, keyboard and mouse actions, and cached HTTP traffic for repeatable task environments. It evaluates agents trained through behavioral cloning and reinforcement learning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. Publisher citation uses Tianlin Shi and Linxi Fan; the PDF also prints the nicknames Tim and Jim. The ordered publisher author names are retained.

name: GUI Testing Using Computer Vision
summary: Presents visual GUI test scripts that use images to specify actions and expected screen feedback. Recording both input events and screenshots can generate tests from demonstrations, supporting unit, regression, and test-driven workflows.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. This is a separate visual-testing contribution from the 2009 Sikuli paper. MIT PDF download returned HTTP 429; its complete institutional abstract and citation metadata remain the retained review source.

name: PLOW: A Collaborative Task Learning Agent
summary: Describes PLOW, which learns executable web-task models from a session combining demonstrations, natural-language explanations, and dialogue. Browser instrumentation connects user actions with DOM structure to support task generalization.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. The ordered names follow the original published paper, without expanding initials or replacing names from secondary indexes.

name: Kite: Building Conversational Bots from Mobile Apps
summary: Derives task graphs from demonstrated Android app interactions and layers a conversational question-answer interface over those graphs. The evaluation examines task-model extraction and developer use of the resulting bot templates.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources.

name: Rousillon: Scraping Distributed Hierarchical Web Data
summary: Introduces Rousillon, which generalizes a demonstration of collecting one hierarchical data row into a browser-automation program that traverses related pages. The paper develops relation-selection and generalization methods and evaluates users building such scripts.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. This is browser interaction learned from demonstrations.

name: Sikuli: Using GUI screenshots for search and automation
summary: Introduces screenshot-based GUI search and visual scripting, using image patterns to locate interface targets and direct mouse and keyboard events. It evaluates screenshot queries and demonstrates automation and interactive-help tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. MIT identifies the retained content as an author final manuscript record. Its PDF download returned HTTP 429; no retry was made. The complete institutional abstract and bibliographic record were read.

name: Rico: A Mobile App Dataset for Building Data-Driven Design Applications
summary: Introduces Rico, collecting Android interface designs and interaction traces through crowdsourced use followed by automated exploration. The paper demonstrates UI-layout retrieval using learned representations and describes visual, textual, structural, and interaction data.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. The paper is a distinct resource from the already cataloged Rico dataset (url:0b134b082a7bd507fc6a). The publisher PDF describes 9.7k apps and 72k screens; the project page describes 9.3k apps and 66k screens. The annotation intentionally supplies no merged size claim.

name: APPINITE: A Multi-Modal Interface for Specifying Data Descriptions in Programming by Demonstration Using Natural Language Instructions
summary: Introduces APPINITE, a conversational interface for specifying the intended targets of demonstrated Android actions. It constructs semantic UI representations and uses an on-screen overlay to preview and refine executable data descriptions.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. The base SUGILITE framework and later PUMICE work are distinct publications; this paper focuses on resolving data-description ambiguity in demonstrations.

name: GUI-SAGE: Enhancing GUI Automation with Self-Explanatory Learning
summary: GUI-SAGE generates reasoning conditioned on known actions and weights policy updates using confidence and reward signals. Its experiments use AndroidControl and GUIOdyssey data and separately evaluate interactive AndroidWorld tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. New work proposal from the official CVF accepted open-access version. No invented day, DOI, or arXiv identifier.

name: Eager: Programming Repetitive Tasks by Example
summary: Describes Eager, which detects repeated HyperCard interactions, generalizes them into loops, and previews predicted actions by highlighting interface objects. Users can then ask it to execute the inferred repetitive task.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. The 1991 conference paper is kept distinct from the 1991 video and 1993/1995 reprints listed on the author project page. Macintosh/HyperCard is tagged desktop.

name: Koala: Capture, Share, Automate, Personalize Business Processes on the Web
summary: Introduces Koala, a collaborative web automation system that records browser interactions as editable pseudo-natural-language scripts. Scripts are shared through a wiki and instantiated with personal or corporate data for reuse by other users.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. This proposal is the specific Koala paper.

name: CowPilot: A Framework for Autonomous and Human-Agent Collaborative Web Navigation
summary: Introduces CowPilot, a web-navigation framework where agents suggest actions and users can pause, reject, override, or resume them. It evaluates autonomous and collaborative use through task success and human effort.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: Why Are Web AI Agents More Vulnerable Than Standalone LLMs? A Security Analysis
summary: Analyzes web-agent vulnerabilities at the component level, examining goal placement in prompts, multistep action generation, and observations as sources of increased susceptibility.
verify_terms: Why Are Web AI Agents Mo
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: The Obvious Invisible Threat: LLM-Powered GUI Agents' Vulnerability to Fine-Print Injections
summary: Characterizes six forms of GUI-content injection and studies their effects on GUI agents and human users using adversarial webpages. The analysis examines privacy failures and the limits of human oversight.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
summary: Introduces UFO2, a Windows desktop agent architecture combining a coordinating HostAgent, application-specialized agents, and a shared GUI/API action layer. It integrates UI Automation, visual parsing, speculative planning, and an isolated picture-in-picture desktop.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
summary: Introduces WASP, an end-to-end benchmark for prompt-injection security in web agents. Its evaluation separates partial attack progress from completion of the attacker’s full objective.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
summary: Guides visual GUI agents at inference time with a process-reward model that evaluates intermediate actions. It combines stepwise guidance with trajectory reflection and retry mechanisms in static and interactive navigation tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: PixelWeb: The First Web GUI Dataset with Pixel-Wise Labels
summary: Introduces PixelWeb, a webpage GUI dataset with element images, contours, and pixel masks. Its annotation pipeline combines bitmap channel information with DOM-based visibility and stacking analysis to address occlusion and overlapping elements.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
summary: Presents a position paper on privacy and security evaluation for GUI agents, identifying risk categories and challenges in involving human evaluators. It proposes risk-aware assessment and in-context consent as design directions.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a position paper proposing an evaluation framework.

name: OSUniverse: Benchmark for Multimodal GUI-navigation AI Agents
summary: Introduces OSUniverse, a desktop GUI benchmark spanning precise clicks through multistep and multiapplication tasks. It provides both manual scoring and an automated validation mechanism.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: Do MLLMs Capture How Interfaces Guide User Behavior? A Benchmark for Multimodal UI/UX Design Understanding
summary: Introduces WiserUI-Bench, pairing real UI variants from industry A/B tests with observed behavioral winners and expert explanations. It evaluates models’ ability to predict the more effective interface and explain its effect on user behavior.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. This benchmark measures UI/UX design understanding from static image pairs.

name: Characterizing Unintended Consequences in Human-GUI Agent Collaboration for Web Browsing
summary: Studies unintended consequences of collaborative web browsing with GUI agents through social-media analysis and interviews. It organizes observed failures, user impacts, and mitigation practices around planning, interface interaction, feedback, privacy, and trust.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Creating General User Models from Computer Use
summary: Proposes general user models that turn computer-use observations into confidence-weighted propositions and revise them as new context arrives. Demonstrations use this memory to contextualize assistants, manage notifications, and support proactive actions across apps.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: EVA: Evolving Semantic Adversaries for Red-Teaming GUI Agents Against Environmental Injection Attacks
summary: Introduces EVA, a red-teaming framework that evolves semantic payloads for GUI environmental-injection tests. It studies the contribution of semantic versus visual deception and distills discovered patterns into reusable evaluation rules.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Studies backdoor risks in mobile GUI agents through AgentGhost, which combines goal-level and interaction-history triggers during model training. The paper evaluates multiple mobile agents and a tailored defense.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ScreenExplorer: Training a Vision-Language Model for Diverse Exploration in Open GUI World
summary: Trains ScreenExplorer with reinforcement learning in dynamic GUI environments, using a world-model curiosity reward and experience-stream distillation to support sustained exploration.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
summary: Studies advertising delivery as an indirect-injection channel for web agents under a black-box threat model. AdInject evaluates how static ad content shaped by website context can redirect browser actions.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: UI-Evol: Automatic Knowledge Evolving for Computer Use Agents
summary: Introduces UI-Evol, which extracts action sequences from agent interactions and critiques external guidance against those traces. Evaluation on OSWorld examines how revised operational knowledge affects execution and behavioral consistency.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: RiOSWorld: Benchmarking the Risk of Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces RiOSWorld, a computer-use risk benchmark separating user-originated and environmental threats. It evaluates both risky-goal intent and goal completion across web and other computer applications.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces VPI-Bench, interactive web-platform variants containing visually embedded malicious instructions. It evaluates computer-use and browser-use agents under these threats and examines system-prompt defenses.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces VerificAgent, which grows domain-specific memories from task trajectories and subjects them to human fact-checking before deployment. Its OSWorld evaluation treats persistent memory as an auditable constraint on later agent behavior.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUIPilot: A Consistency-based Mobile GUI Testing Approach for Detecting Application-specific Bugs
summary: Introduces GUIPilot, which compares mobile design mock-ups with implemented screens through widget alignment and tests expected transitions by executing inferred UI actions. It evaluates both visual inconsistencies and workflow-specific bugs.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments
summary: Introduces EconWebArena, a curated benchmark of economic-data tasks requiring live website navigation, multimodal interpretation, and precise extraction. It evaluates visual grounding, planning, and interaction design within multistep workflows.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: UITron-Speech: Towards Automated GUI Agents Based on Speech Instructions
summary: Introduces UITron-Speech, which predicts GUI actions from spoken instructions and screenshots. It combines synthetic speech data and mixed-modality training with a training-free grounding refinement step.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Context manipulation attacks : Web agents are susceptible to corrupted memory
summary: Studies context manipulation in web agents by altering stored task representations. Evaluation on Browser-use and Agent-E examines memory-directed attacks and the implications for secure context handling.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Mobile GUI Agents under Real-world Threats: Are We There Yet?
summary: Introduces an app-content instrumentation framework and complementary interactive and static test suites for mobile GUI agents. It studies how untrusted third-party content changes task execution and state understanding.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: A Systematization of Security Vulnerabilities in Computer Use Agents
summary: Analyzes security boundaries in computer-use agents through a risk taxonomy and concrete adversarial case studies. It links observed failures to input provenance, interface-action binding, memory, and delegation, and proposes CUA-specific evaluation principles.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a threat analysis with case studies.

name: VisualTrap: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack on GUI Agents via Visual Grounding Manipulation
summary: Studies backdoors that redirect GUI visual grounding even when the task plan is correct. VisualTrap evaluates whether poisoned grounding training transfers to downstream tasks and across web, mobile, and desktop interface settings.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LaSM, a training-free defense that selectively scales attention and MLP components to improve alignment with task-relevant screen regions. It evaluates the approach against pop-up-based GUI injection attacks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
summary: Introduces WebGuard, a human-annotated dataset for predicting outcomes and risk levels of state-changing website actions. It provides generalization splits and evaluates specialized guardrail models.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree
summary: Studies indirect prompt injection through HTML content consumed as accessibility trees. The evaluation tests how manipulated page observations redirect browser-agent actions on real websites.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces GuirlVG, an empirical study of reinforcement fine-tuning for GUI visual grounding. It analyzes training components and adds an adaptive KL-based mechanism to limit reward over-optimization.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
summary: Introduces Morae, a UI agent that detects decision points and pauses for user choices using interface code and screenshots. A study with blind and low-vision participants evaluates this mixed-initiative approach on real web tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: MobiAgent: A Systematic Framework for Customizable Mobile Agents
summary: Presents MobiAgent, combining MobiMind agent models, the AgentRR acceleration framework, and MobiFlow evaluation. It also introduces an AI-assisted data-collection pipeline for mobile GUI tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: SparkUI-Parser: Enhancing GUI Perception with Robust Grounding and Parsing
summary: Introduces SparkUI-Parser, which adds continuous coordinate decoding and a rejection mechanism for nonexistent targets to a multimodal model. It also presents ScreenParse for evaluating structural interface perception.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: VeriOS: Query-Driven Proactive Human-Agent-GUI Interaction for Trustworthy OS Agents
summary: Introduces VeriOS-Agent, which learns when to execute GUI actions autonomously and when to query a user under untrustworthy conditions. Its staged training combines supervised learning and group-relative policy optimization.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces AgentSentinel, which intercepts sensitive computer-agent operations and audits them using task context together with system traces. BadComputerUse evaluates this enforcement approach across attack scenarios involving tool and computer control.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The official full paper confirms GUI/desktop interaction alongside Bash and file tools. Its abstract and body enumerate attack categories differently; no category count is promoted into this annotation.

name: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
summary: Studies how GUI agents, people, and human-agent teams respond to manipulative interface designs. The two-phase evaluation examines failure modes and the benefits and costs of human oversight.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
summary: Introduces Chameleon, an environmental-injection evaluation framework that varies webpage content and trigger context. It combines simulated page variation with attention-based optimization and tests GUI agents across realistic websites.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
summary: Introduces PrivWeb, which uses a local language model to anonymize interface information according to user preferences. Adaptive notifications and selective pauses give users control over sensitive information access during web-agent tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: See, Think, Act: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Effectively Interact with GUI by Identifying Toggles
summary: Introduces a benchmark for binary GUI-toggle instructions and State-aware Reasoning, which compares the observed control state with the requested state before choosing an action. It evaluates agents on toggle tasks and broader interactive benchmarks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.

name: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
summary: Introduces MobileRisk-Live and OS-Sentinel, combining a formal verifier for system-level violations with a multimodal judge for contextual risks in mobile GUI workflows.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Hi-Agent: Hierarchical Vision-Language Agents for Mobile Device Control
summary: Introduces Hi-Agent, jointly training a high-level reasoning model and a low-level mobile action model. Execution feedback supplies a foresight advantage for optimizing subgoal decisions, with evaluations on Android control benchmarks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. This Hi-Agent has a distinct author team and method from the earlier HiAgent working-memory paper.

name: ReInAgent: A Context-Aware GUI Agent Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Mobile Task Navigation
summary: Introduces ReInAgent, coordinating information management, planning, and reflection around a shared memory for mobile tasks. It proactively asks users for information and checks consistency when instructions are ambiguous or change during execution.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces GUI Exploration Lab, a simulation engine for composing screens, interface elements, and navigation graphs. It studies how supervised learning, single-turn RL, and multiturn RL affect GUI navigation and exploration.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MobileDreamer: Generative Sketch World Model for GUI Agent
summary: MobileDreamer predicts post-action GUI states as task-relevant textual sketches with an order-invariant learning objective. Agents use these predictions for lookahead action selection, evaluated on AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
summary: NOVA separates trusted task planning from screen-derived observations by producing a branching plan before execution and resolving runtime values through perception. Its OSWorld study examines security and utility while identifying remaining risks from perception-driven branch steering.
verify_terms: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: Sy
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GraphPilot: GUI Task Automation with One-Step LLM Reasoning Powered by Knowledge Graph
summary: GraphPilot builds app-specific knowledge graphs from explored pages, elements and transitions, then uses them to plan action sequences. It requests additional interface observations when uncertain and checks plans against graph transition rules before correction and execution.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.
