name: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents
summary: This study examines UI changes between a desktop agent’s screenshot observation and action dispatch. Its pre-execution state checks address overlay and focus manipulation, while the reported DOM-injection blind spot limits the defense’s coverage.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing that changed action preferences can coexist with unchanged held-out accuracy.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation
summary: The framework uses a vision-language judge’s final-screen assessment as a terminal reward for GUI reinforcement learning. It models evaluator noise and corrects the reward estimator used by PPO across desktop benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Any Customized UI
summary: EmbeWebAgent embeds agent access into existing web applications through frontend observations and a page-specific function registry. Its workflow combines GUI primitives, composite actions and MCP tools, demonstrated in a live interface.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
summary: GUICrafter first learns grounding from large collections of unannotated screenshots and webpages, then uses a smaller high-quality dataset for reinforcement-learning calibration. The curriculum targets reduced dependence on manually annotated GUI training data.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
summary: DragOn supplies drag-grounding training data and a held-out benchmark for highlighting text, selecting cells, resizing elements and moving sliders. It evaluates existing vision-language models and a model fine-tuned on the drag tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Training Computer Use Agents to Assess the Usability of Graphical User Interfaces
summary: uxCUA learns to assess interface usability by choosing interaction flows, executing them and predicting a numerical usability score. Training uses interactive UIs with usability labels and human preferences, with evaluations on synthetic and real interfaces.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.
verify_terms: Invisible in Space, Visible in T
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Gated Hindsight Distillation gives a teacher access to the next screenshot during training while the student sees only the available trajectory prefix. Distillation is applied when hindsight repairs a student failure, and the resulting policies are evaluated on Android tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: "Allow" to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
summary: This permission-literacy study tests whether mobile GUI agents grant only task-necessary permissions. Controlled changes to task context and requester identity expose authorization biases and the trade-off between suppressing unnecessary and legitimate grants.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
summary: This benchmark matches desktop goals, initial states and final-state verifiers across screen-only GUI and skill-mediated CLI agents. Its experiments separate graphical execution failures from missing CLI skill coverage, including a verifier-guided skill-augmentation condition.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks
summary: ChainWorld composes compatible atomic OSWorld tasks into multi-objective desktop chains while preserving their evaluators. It compares giving the full sequence at once with revealing goals turn by turn, exposing different state and session-management failures.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.
verify_terms: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enoug
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MacArena: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on an Online macOS Environment
summary: MacArena runs computer-use tasks through Apple’s virtualization framework on Apple Silicon, combining task ports with macOS-native workloads. It distinguishes the ported and native subsets when examining agent performance and cross-platform transfer.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.
verify_terms: Online Skill Learning for Web Ag
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
summary: CLI-Anything argues for application interfaces built around structured commands, explicit state and execution feedback. It describes transforming existing software into command-line harnesses and organizing that approach through CLI-Hub.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent computer-interface architecture: the described application command harnesses concern computer operation, but no GUI execution or comparative benchmark result is established in the abstract.

name: Multi-Agent Computer Use
summary: MACU represents computer-use objectives as a dependency graph whose manager dispatches parallel subagents and revises tasks as new information arrives. Desktop and web experiments examine coordination, information handoff and task-completion time.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents
summary: UI-KOBE explores mobile applications to build graphs of UI states and executable transitions. A lightweight agent then matches its current screenshot to the graph and chooses a transition, local action, completion signal or fallback action.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
summary: MobileExplorer probes relevant UI elements while an on-device model is reasoning, then supplies the exploration trace as compact context. A two-level rollback mechanism restores the working state when simple backtracking fails.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
summary: DRS-GUI searches screenshot regions through focus, shift and scatter operations selected by a tree-search planner. A region-quality reward guides this training-free perceptual search before final GUI grounding.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.
notes: The complete retained official abstract and cached official README were reviewed.

name: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
summary: ToolCUA synthesizes interleaved GUI/tool trajectories and trains agents to choose between graphical actions and higher-level tools. Staged supervised and reinforcement learning culminate in online hybrid-environment training with a reward for efficient execution paths.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Do LLMs Need to See Everything? A Benchmark and Study of Failures in LLM-driven Smartphone Automation using Screentext vs. Screenshots
summary: DailyDroid compares text-only and text-plus-screenshot agents on everyday Android tasks across multiple apps and difficulty levels. Its failure analysis examines accessibility, observation modality and agent/application behavior.
verify_terms: Do LLMs Need to See Everything?
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
summary: This study examines repeated OSWorld executions to separate execution stochasticity, task-specification ambiguity and behavioral variation. Paired task-level tests show why one successful run is insufficient evidence of reliable computer use.
verify_terms: On the Reliability of Computer U
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
summary: UI-Copilot separates GUI execution from on-demand memory retrieval and numerical assistance. Its training procedure treats tool selection and multi-turn task execution as distinct optimization targets while keeping persistent observations outside transient context.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.
verify_terms: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? A
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.
verify_terms: Learn How to Act from Your Own I
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
summary: BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
summary: Confidence-Anchored Learning uses coordinate-token confidence to filter pseudo-supervision for GUI grounding. Its negative-only variant performs label-free test-time updates to reduce reliance on potentially incorrect positive examples.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
summary: AgentHijack evaluates whether visual patch effects propagate from screenshots through model outputs and action parsing into real environment changes. Its controlled web-page experiments distinguish intermediate attack signals from verified end-to-end consequences.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
summary: SynWeaver explores a website to build a map of page states and executable interactions, then learns website priors for task proposals. Joint task/trajectory synthesis revises inconsistent pairs and verifies or repairs the resulting supervision.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
summary: This framework separates frozen-model instruction expansion from a trained layout-aware matcher that localizes GUI elements without coordinate regression. Binary text/icon supervision supports the matcher, with evaluations on GUI grounding and Mind2Web element-selection tasks.

summary: OpenAgents hosts three language agents, for data analysis, API plugins and autonomous web browsing, behind a web interface for non-expert users, with local deployment for developers.

summary: GUI-CIDER turns GUI trajectories into textual planning and causal interface knowledge, reselects exemplars for causal structure and low redundancy, then mid-trains GUI agents on that corpus.

summary: FingerTip 20K gathers 20K human Android demonstrations from users' long-term everyday app use, with user context, to evaluate proactive task suggestion and preference-aware task execution.

name: Pix2Struct: Screenshot Parsing as Pretraining for Visual Language Understanding
summary: Pix2Struct pretrains an image-to-text model by reconstructing simplified HTML from masked webpage screenshots. Its variable-resolution visual representation is evaluated across several domains, including user-interface understanding.

summary: UISCGD detects semantic groups of adjacent text and non-text UI elements. It learns from Android and iOS screenshots to support interface retrieval, UI-to-code structure and screen-reader accessibility.

name: MUD: Towards a Large-Scale and Noise-Filtered UI Dataset for Modern Style UI Modeling

summary: MUD combines LLM-guided Android app exploration, noise filtering and human annotation to collect modern UI screenshots. The study evaluates the resulting data for element detection and UI retrieval.

summary: Orienter detects interactable GUI elements in XR applications by interpreting scene context and revisiting candidate elements through a validation and reflection loop. It addresses open-vocabulary element types and context-dependent interactability.

name: Generalist Virtual Agents: A Survey on Autonomous Agents Across Digital Platforms
summary: Surveys virtual agents for browsers, applications and operating systems, organizing prior work by task type, observation and action spaces, model strategies and evaluation methods. It examines screen-based interaction and keyboard, mouse and touch control, alongside transferability and long-sequence decision-making challenges.

name: In-Context Defense in Computer Agents: An Empirical Study

verify_terms: A Survey of WebAgents: Towards Next-Gene

name: EcoAgent: An Efficient Device-Cloud Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Mobile Automation
summary: EcoAgent splits mobile automation between cloud planning and on-device observation and verification. Compact screen descriptions and feedback reduce communication costs, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

name: LLM-Explorer: Towards Efficient and Affordable LLM-based Exploration for Mobile Apps
summary: LLM-Explorer uses language models to maintain compact knowledge for mobile app exploration, then generates actions without invoking the model at every step. The study compares exploration coverage and cost across twenty apps.
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.

name: Unlocking Smarter Device Control: Foresighted Planning with a World Model-Driven Code Execution Approach
summary: FPWC builds and refines a task-oriented world model before planning mobile-device actions. It executes plans as code and evaluates the approach in simulated environments and on real mobile devices.
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.

name: XBOUND: Exploring Capability Boundaries of Device-Control Agents at the State Level
summary: XBOUND evaluates GUI agents at the level of a screen state, considering multiple instructions and possible target actions within it. The study separates action matching from instruction unification and compares effects of grounding and trajectory data.

name: Open CaptchaWorld: A Comprehensive Web-based Platform for Testing and Benchmarking Multimodal LLM Agents
summary: Open CaptchaWorld evaluates multimodal agents on interactive browser-based CAPTCHA puzzles. Its benchmark distinguishes task success from the depth of visual reasoning and interaction needed to complete a puzzle.

summary: DeepShop evaluates shopping agents with evolving query complexity across product attributes, filters and sorting preferences. Its evaluation combines checks of these individual requirements with overall task success.

name: Scenario-Guided LLM-based Mobile App GUI Testing
summary: ScenGen organizes mobile GUI testing around business scenarios. Five collaborating agents observe the interface, choose and execute actions, check scenario completion, and record operations and runtime bugs.

name: Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction

name: NaviMaster: Learning a Unified Policy for GUI and Embodied Navigation Tasks

summary: NaviMaster trains a shared policy for GUI and embodied navigation using a common visual-trajectory formulation. It combines trajectory collection, reinforcement learning and distance-aware rewards, with evaluation across both task families.

name: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
verify_terms: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detect
summary: MANA combines visual, temporal and exploration signals to guide navigation toward mobile advertisements. It evaluates ad detection and interaction cost on commercial smartphones, including obfuscated-ad cases.

name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

name: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
summary: Measures the complementarity, cost and rerun variability of six browser observation modes on WebArena and VisualWebArena. Its routing experiments distinguish an oracle cost opportunity from policies that fail to robustly outperform a fixed observation mode.

name: LoginTrap: Uncovering Task-Agnostic Phishing-Style Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks against LLM-based Web Agents
summary: Introduces LoginTrap, a black-box indirect-injection evaluation in which attacker-controlled page context and login flows induce unauthorized authentication. It measures end-to-end private-data leakage across web-agent backbones, architectures and defenses.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
summary: GUI-Lens uses OCR and detected interface components as coordinate references while a general-purpose VLM selects progressively enlarged screenshot crops. Instruction-conditioned checks constrain the crop and click proposals before mapping the final location back to the original screen.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
summary: MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
summary: CUADebug combines a failure taxonomy and human-annotated OSWorld failure trajectories with an agent that locates causal steps and proposes corrections from screenshots and action traces. It evaluates root-cause diagnosis separately from controlled task re-execution and failure recovery.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
summary: OpenForgeRL connects stateful agent harnesses to reinforcement-learning infrastructure through a model-call recording proxy and isolated rollout containers. Its validation includes browser and computer-use agents, alongside tool-oriented agents, and examines how harness choice affects learned reliability.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Beyond Sequential Interaction: Benchmarking Parallel Execution and Coordination for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces ParaGUIBench, with tasks and efficiency measurements for coordinated GUI agents operating separate desktop instances over a shared file system. Its ParaGUI planner-worker system decomposes tasks and dispatches concurrent subtasks for comparison with serial execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
summary: EvoCUA-1.5 trains multi-turn desktop agents through online reinforcement learning in executable sandboxes. It combines step-level policy optimization, task filtering and calibration, an adaptive curriculum, and asynchronous rollout handling with staleness control.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure
summary: Defines visual state reliance and probes whether GUI agents resolve screenshot/structure conflicts using pixels, serialized interface structure or prior beliefs. Paired interventions and live multi-step tests connect misattributed state beliefs to failures and compare consistency-based mitigations.
verify_terms: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
summary: LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets
summary: Argus benchmarks post-hoc uncertainty methods for single-step GUI grounding across open-weight and closed-source observation regimes. It tests calibration, rejection, error severity and conformal click regions, finding that uncertainty rankings transfer less reliably across model/interface regimes than across datasets for one model.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding
summary: WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: ENVS branches over GUI actions in live desktop VMs, verifies successful leaves, and converts them into balanced step-level training supervision. It also introduces OSWorld-Noisy to test recovery from dynamic interruptions while retaining the underlying tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MobileForge: Annotation-Free Adaptation for Mobile GUI Agents with Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization
summary: MobileForge couples real-app exploration and generated tasks with hierarchical feedback for mobile-agent adaptation. Its optimizer turns trajectory outcomes, step feedback and corrective hints into contextualized GRPO updates, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and a GUI-only MobileWorld split.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for GUI coordinate generation under student-produced prefixes. A correctness-aware gate suppresses coordinate-token supervision outside the target box, while teacher-probability scaling adjusts the remaining signal strength.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents
summary: VISUALSKILL organizes application-specific text and figures into hierarchical skills retrieved on demand through an MCP tool. Skills combine authored documentation with live UI exploration, and matched multimodal/text-only comparisons test their utility for interface identification and workflow-state verification.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection
summary: FraudSMSWalker tests browser agents on bilingual SMS-to-webpage fraud judgments while hiding URL and reputation shortcuts. Its controlled chains include difficult benign login/payment cases and evaluate whether classifications remain supported by the visible message and page evidence.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VISTA: View-Consistent Self-Verified Training for GUI Grounding
summary: VISTA forms GRPO comparison groups from target-preserving crops of the same GUI instance with exactly remapped target boxes. A conditional, advantage-weighted cross-view anchor supplies additional supervision without entering the group baseline, and evaluation includes view-consistency robustness.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
summary: PhoneHarness routes phone workflows across GUI actions, device-side commands and host tools while retaining auditable execution traces. Its accompanying benchmark checks observable task side effects, separating mixed-action execution from plausible final-answer generation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
summary: Introduces CUA-HandCrafted, a browser-agent red-teaming benchmark that varies attack templates, tasks and system prompts. Its domain comparison and reproducibility audit caution against transferring browser-surface safety conclusions to coding agents or unreleased optimized injections.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content
summary: MIRAGE constructs mobile screenshot injections in ordinary user-content regions through localization, contextual payload generation and realism curation. Its evaluation separates visual realism from attack effectiveness against pixel-observing GUI agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
summary: PlaytestArena evaluates generated browser games using expected in-play behaviors adjudicated by GUI agents. Play2Code pairs a coding agent with a rubric-blind GUI playtester whose interaction traces and feedback guide iterative refinement, with a separate final judge.
verify_terms: GUI Agents for Continual Game Ge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. GUI agents actually load and play browser-game builds, providing an executable interface-testing signal for game-code generation; the central application remains game development.

name: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution
summary: MaskClaw makes local Allow, Mask or Ask decisions before GUI screenshots leave a trusted environment, using visual evidence and personalized policy memory. Its benchmark and designed evolution scenarios test how corrections and edits can become privacy skills checked by a sandbox gate.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AndroidDaily: A Verifiable Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents on Real-World Closed-Source Applications
summary: AndroidDaily evaluates mobile GUI agents on daily workflows in closed-source Android apps. Its GRADE evaluator follows visual trajectories against operational obligations, output-quality requirements and negative constraints, producing process-level diagnostics without hidden app state.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling
summary: Agent JIT compilation turns browser task descriptions into validated executable plans containing model calls, tools and parallel work. A cost-based scheduler and pre/postcondition protocol target latency and incorrect tool use in web-agent execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: DocOS: Towards Proactive Document-Guided Actions in GUI Agents
summary: DocOS benchmarks agents that search online documentation and translate procedural instructions into GUI actions in interactive web environments. It separates failures to retrieve useful procedures from failures to ground retrieved instructions into executable actions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. It also converts computer-use traces into controller training data and evaluates semantic actions, progress and memory consistency on long-horizon tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: TClone: Low-Latency Forking of Live GUI Environments for Computer-Use Agents
summary: TClone versions live GUI workspaces through snapshots, isolated forks, rollback and selective commit or merge. It separates fast branch creation from durable checkpoints using copy-on-write sharing, filesystem versioning and asynchronous checkpointing, with end-to-end agent-loop latency measurements.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm
summary: Argues for compiling web tasks into predefined execution graphs before exposing an agent to untrusted runtime content. Its WebArena task analysis identifies typed, semantically complete website tools as a prerequisite and distinguishes this interface proposal from reactive click-level control.
verify_terms: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Directly analyzes browser-agent prompt-injection boundaries and WebArena task structure, advocating typed website operations.

name: WinDeskGround: A Benchmark for Robust GUI Grounding in Complex Multi-Window Desktop Environments
summary: WinDeskGround synthesizes multi-window desktop layouts with controlled occlusion, density and semantic similarity to test GUI grounding robustness. Its instruction-target benchmark measures how localization changes when interfaces depart from simple single-layer scenes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
summary: Executable Agentic Memory stores GUI routines in a knowledge graph built through state-aware exploration and action-group mining. A learned value model guides tree search over this executable memory for retrieval-based planning, with AndroidWorld and efficiency evaluation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
summary: Introduces CUActSpot to evaluate clicks, drags, drawing and other screen interactions across GUI, text, tables, canvases and natural images. A renderer-based pipeline records geometry and screenshots, then generates matching instructions and action traces for training a grounding model.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Don't Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces
summary: DUDE combines asymmetric hybrid-reward learning with summaries of deceptive-interface failures to guide safer web actions. Its RUC benchmark evaluates deception susceptibility alongside ordinary task performance across interface scenarios.
verify_terms: Don't Click That: Teaching Web A
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
summary: A11y-Compressor transforms linearized accessibility trees through modal detection, redundancy reduction and semantic structuring. Its OSWorld evaluation measures both observation-token reduction and task success.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
summary: Proposes a step-level model cascade that runs a smaller computer-use policy until learned monitors flag stalled progress or semantic drift. Separate history-based stuck detection and milestone checks determine when to escalate for recovery or verification without retraining the larger model.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AutoSurfer -- Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
summary: AutoSurfer explores website actions breadth-first, retaining page and trajectory knowledge to guide task synthesis and trajectory refinement. It evaluates the resulting training data by fine-tuning a web agent on WebArena and examining synthesized-task diversity.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AutoGUI-v2: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal GUI Functionality Understanding Benchmark
summary: AutoGUI-v2 evaluates interface functionality, grounding and predicted interaction outcomes using hierarchical regions derived through VLM-human annotation. Its tasks span multiple operating systems and expose differences between functional localization, captioning and transition-logic understanding.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VLAA-GUI: Knowing When to Stop, Recover, and Search, A Modular Framework for GUI Automation
summary: VLAA-GUI combines mandatory checks for visually supported completion, multi-tier loop recovery and on-demand workflow search. Optional coding and grounding agents support execution, with component ablations on Linux and Windows GUI tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebUncertainty: Dual-Level Uncertainty Driven Planning and Reasoning For Autonomous Web Agent
summary: WebUncertainty adapts planning mode to task uncertainty and guides action-level tree search with confidence-derived uncertainty estimates. Its evaluations examine autonomous execution of dynamic, long-horizon web tasks on WebArena and WebVoyager.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agents for In-Situ Assistance via Live Interface Transformation
summary: DOMSteer translates help requests and live page context into reversible DOM changes such as control highlighting, contextual tooltips and layout reorganization. The work evaluates in-place GUI assistance with interface tests, use cases and a comparative user study.
verify_terms: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agen
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents
summary: WebXSkill pairs parameterized action programs with step-level language guidance, mining reusable skills from synthetic browser-agent traces. A URL-based graph supports retrieval, and deployment alternates between direct program execution and guided native planning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
summary: EE-MCP studies application-dependent mixtures of GUI actions and MCP calls using generated environments, trajectory collection and filtered training. An experience bank extracts rules from trajectory comparisons for inference-time improvement, distinct from model distillation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis
summary: GUIDE evaluates GUI trajectories by segmenting them into subtasks, diagnosing each segment, and aggregating structured findings into a task verdict. It tests diagnostic judgments on e-commerce, web-agent and Android-control traces.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
summary: OmniGUI evaluates step-level action prediction from interleaved smartphone screenshots, synchronous audio and video. Expert demonstrations carry multimodal-dependency annotations, and initial baselines use native multimodal models as agent proxies to study temporal and audio-related failures.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic Web Agents via State Machine Memory
summary: ActionEngine explores web applications to build an updateable state-machine memory of GUI states, operations and transitions. It generates complete task programs from that memory, using reactive repair to handle changed interfaces or missing knowledge.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
summary: OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: UI-Oceanus: Scaling GUI Agents with Synthetic Environmental Dynamics
summary: UI-Oceanus converts autonomous GUI exploration and execution feedback into supervision for predicting future interface states. It compares forward and inverse objectives during continual pretraining and examines downstream offline and online navigation as synthetic data scales.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles
summary: LongPuzzleBench evaluates coherent long-horizon planning on persistent visual puzzle boards through native GUI actions. It compares GUI-only and code-assisted agents and uses controlled hints and memory diagnostics to examine decisions that preserve or eliminate future solutions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Agents execute real GUI moves in six puzzle games; the tasks diagnose computer-control planning in game-based workflows.

name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.
verify_terms: The Hard Part Comes After Search
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.
verify_terms: Guides That Cause Actions: An Of
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
summary: MaP unifies GUI-navigation objectives by masking and predicting components of multi-turn trajectories. Role-aware adapters address heterogeneous training data, and evaluations compare the approach with direct task-mixture training across navigation benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
summary: PACE weights coordinate-digit entropy by place value to estimate confidence in GUI clicks from one forward pass. It evaluates correctness ranking and selective accuracy against repeated-sampling alternatives on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.
verify_terms: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
summary: MintAct trains a visual-agent family for grounding, navigation and tool use across mobile, desktop and web environments. Its shared infrastructure supports trajectory collection and asynchronous online RL while controlling cross-domain sampling and off-policy drift.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents
summary: Studies how automatic defaults and reflective social-influence cues affect GUI-agent shopping decisions under different reasoning configurations. A randomized simulated-shopping experiment finds that reasoning changes the type of susceptibility.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
summary: Investigates mismatches between what humans see on a mobile display and what agents receive through screenshots or accessibility metadata. An automated evaluation framework embeds instruction-agnostic perturbations into functional APK clones and compares static and dynamic agent deviations with human noticeability.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
summary: OdoBot builds a model of web-application behavior from successful task demonstrations and uses it to guide task execution. Its Canvas LMS evaluation compares token use and completion with existing web agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
summary: JarvisGUI composes typed input-output task transformations into dynamic workflows spanning Android, Windows and Ubuntu devices. Its virtual-environment benchmark tests transfer of intermediate results, shared state and cross-device dependencies.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams
summary: Introduces activation-conditioned gradient control for GUI agents learning successive applications. It protects inactive application-specific neurons, constrains updates to shared neurons, and accumulates a compact historical state to balance adaptation with retention.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Do GUI Agents Know When Not to Act? Enabling Conflict-Aware Termination for Multimodal GUI Agents
summary: CONFLICTGUI evaluates termination under instruction conflicts and mismatches between instructions and interface context. CONFLICTGUARD couples feasibility checks with conditional action modulation to reduce unnecessary execution while tracking normal-task behavior.
verify_terms: Do GUI Agents Know When Not to A
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision
summary: Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
summary: LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection
summary: LookAgain treats a GUI coordinate as a revisable hypothesis, rendering its marker and a local screenshot patch before confirmation. Reflective supervised trajectories provide a cold start, followed by GRPO using terminal grounding correctness.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
summary: CAP builds cross-site browser workflows by decomposing websites into operation and perception requirements and recomposing them into tasks. Its judge-based evaluation diagnoses complex interactions and visual-perception failures across real websites.
verify_terms: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Ev
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MissClick: Execution-Aware Adversarial Attacks on Coordinate Generation in GUI Grounding Models
summary: MissClick designs white-box attacks around the numerical effect of coordinate digits on executable GUI clicks. Separate untargeted displacement and targeted place-weighted objectives are evaluated across desktop, web and mobile grounding settings.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
summary: KnowAct-GUIClaw combines a host planner with pluggable GUI subagents, attributable experience memory and an evolving skill library. It uses user profiles and feedback for task decomposition and evaluates transfer across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS and Windows.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism
summary: Studies a controlled setting where GRPO fails to improve a strong small web agent and can reduce text-track performance. Matched reachable-reward tasks and component grafting distinguish limited optimization headroom from learning-rate-dependent failure mechanisms.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure
summary: StructAgent maintains compact task state and regulates long-horizon execution through verified transitions and progress checkpoints. Its workflow supports evidence-based completion and targeted recovery, with desktop computer-use evaluation and a separate Minecraft extension.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
summary: MAG jointly evaluates browser task actions and user-facing guides grounded in screenshots through element marks or pixel coordinates. Its harness covers annotation, live evaluation and joint metrics, with an expert-trajectory-augmented GRPO training study.
verify_terms: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and H
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
summary: WebRetriever evaluates navigation, knowledge-assisted interaction and end-to-end information-extraction workflows under separate protocols. Its NavEval judge uses richer interaction context to diagnose cases where navigation success and useful task completion diverge.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees
summary: Untrusted Content Masking uses DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before agent observation. A sandboxed interaction interface separates privileges so browser actions can proceed under the proposed trust-boundary model without exposing protected content to the planner.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Uses failed computer-use trajectories to diagnose failure modes and generate inference-time agent code patches, with light human verification. An OSWorld study evaluates this failure-driven improvement loop without additional model training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: On the Internet, Nobody Knows You're an LLM Bot: Unmasking Web Agents with Multi-Layer Fingerprinting
summary: Evaluates web agents against anti-bot mechanisms on instrumented honeysites and analyzes network, HTTP and browser fingerprints. The study compares resistance to blocking with the ability to distinguish agents, humans and agent implementations.
verify_terms: On the Internet, Nobody Knows Yo
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
summary: PEEU explores web environments and turns hindsight experience into aligned high-level planning supervision. A hierarchical task-decomposition analysis examines why atomic-skill competence alone falls short of planning generalization across websites.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
summary: VisCritic compares before/after screenshots through change-aware visual features and an action-conditioned critic. Weakly supervised samples from existing traces train judgments of action success, progress and error type for GUI-agent verification.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
summary: Segments and clusters GUI trajectories into inspectable skills, then trains a skill-aware policy from those annotations. Its diagnostic results distinguish readable source-domain clusters from reliable transfer and report limited or absent downstream gains.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
summary: Builds a logging framework that combines network/protocol fingerprints with browser interaction behavior to attribute web-agent traffic. A decision-tree classifier is evaluated across six agent implementations, human browsing and conventional crawlers.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
summary: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation first lets a policy reach its own off-trajectory states, then uses skill guidance to collect successful continuations. Mixing those continuations with expert traces supplies supervision for recovery states absent from demonstrations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: A grader model extracts the final answer from the response and judges it correct or incorrect against the decrypted reference answer; accuracy is the share judged correct. The reference implementation sends each question to any sampler and does not prescribe browsing tools or an action space.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The count is the number of data rows in the released CSV, whose problem and answer fields are XOR-encrypted with a per-row canary and carry a problem_topic label. Results depend on the agent's browsing tools, the grader model and the number of repeats; record these with a score.

value.basis: Repository LICENSE for the simple-evals code, including the BrowseComp reference implementation; not a declaration for the question data.

name: Scout
summary: TypeScript browser agent that drives any Chromium over CDP in a look-act-check loop, with separate user-chosen hands, brain, eyes and extract models and optional JSON Schema answers.
notes: Published by Outcrawl; the GitHub description calls the repository an automatic mirror of Outcrawl's production repository. Packages: scout (entry point), runtime (agent loop), model (prompts and provider-neutral clients), scout-core, scout-cdp (DevTools-protocol driver) and agenthands (local pointer and keyboard planning). It runs against a local browser, any CDP endpoint or Outcrawl's hosted browser, which needs an Outcrawl key and adds residential connections, captcha solving and replays. The README reports 92.5% page reach on Browser Use's 80-site benchmark. Root code is Apache-2.0; packages/agenthands keeps its own MIT license.

details.availability: Public source and the @outcrawl/scout npm package; the optional hosted browser is a metered Outcrawl service with a free monthly credit allowance

name: typesafe-computer-use
summary: Computer-use loop that reads the screen with OCR and accessibility labels, has the hosted TypeSafe classifier choose each next action with a confidence, and calls a writer model only for free text.
notes: Also called jev. The main loop drives macOS through Vision OCR, the accessibility tree and synthetic input; the Windows adapter (UI Automation, SendInput, Windows OCR) is documented as experimental and untested on Windows. An opt-in browser backend reads the DOM over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and the Linux sandbox runs only that backend. Linux desktop control is through the OSWorld JevAgent adapter inside OSWorld's Ubuntu VM. Every decision calls the hosted TypeSafe API, so a TypeSafe key is required; an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible writer is optional. Per-step cost and latency comparisons and the OSWorld run logs are the author's. The README marks the project beta.

details.availability: Public source; the v0.2.0 GitHub release carries no binary assets; the hosted TypeSafe decision API is required

name: PokeClaw
summary: Android app that runs a phone-control agent on the device, reading the UI tree through an Accessibility service and tapping, swiping and typing with on-device Gemma 4 or an optional cloud model.
notes: Also called PocketClaw. The task loop runs inside the installed APK; ADB control from a host is outside this architecture. Local mode runs Gemma 4 through LiteRT-LM after a model download of about 2.6 GB; Cloud mode calls a hosted model. The tool registry also has notification, clipboard, call, file and knowledge-base tools, plus a separate D-pad tool set for Android TV devices. The README reports pass rates, for example 18 of 20 cloud tasks on a Pixel 8 Pro, from the author's trials.

details.availability: Public source and APK builds attached to GitHub releases

name: UI-TARS 72B SFT
summary: SFT-labelled 72B UI-TARS checkpoint: a native GUI agent model in the Qwen2-VL architecture, stored in FP32, for screen perception, element grounding and multi-step actions on web, mobile and desktop.

name: PhoneCLI
summary: Mobile-agent harness that crawls an app into a YAML map of screens, replays compiled navigation commands through WebDriverAgent on iOS or ADB on Android, and falls back to a VLM for unseen screens.
notes: Formerly published as HKUDS/OpenPhone; that address now resolves to this repository. phonecli/ is the iOS harness (WebDriverAgent) with prebuilt app maps, and phonecli_android/ runs the AndroidLab suite with compiled maps and a pure-VLM baseline. The repository also holds OpenPhone-3B training and synthetic-data pipelines and vLLM serving scripts; the weights and dataset are separate Hugging Face releases outside this repository record. Its evaluation replaces AndroidLab's rule-based checks with an LLM judge. The LICENSE names AndroidLab's author as a copyright holder.

details.availability: Public source; no GitHub releases; OpenPhone-3B weights and dataset are separate Hugging Face repositories

name: Browser Use Desktop

Engines are pluggable adapters in the main process (claude-code is the default; codex and browsercode adapters are also present), and the tree bundles a Browser Harness JavaScript SDK and domain-skill notes for 68 sites. Agent quality depends on the user's Anthropic or OpenAI subscription or API key. The latest non-prerelease is v0.0.31 (2026-05-09) while development continues on main.

name: TipTour

Gemini mode receives microphone audio and, when enabled, screenshots. Video tours are built by the Elorian service and only point at controls. The localhost harness on 127.0.0.1:19474 exposes observe, ground-target and act endpoints. Requires macOS 14.2+ and an Xcode build; the repository has no releases. The MIT LICENSE also credits Farza's Clicky, the upstream fork source; bundled Neko sprites carry a BSD-2-Clause file.

name: CUGA

The README cites arXiv 2510.23856 for its WebArena result; that paper is not in the catalog, and the curated arxiv:2503.01861 describes the CUGA system without naming this repository, so no relation is recorded.

The main-branch Hub manifest holds one Ultralytics weight file, best.pt, and the card gives a 1280-pixel fine-tuning resolution.
