GroundingOracle.swift resolves targets for the Mimicry replay system in four steps: exact accessibility-tree match, fuzzy accessibility match, a local ShowUI-2B model on MLX over a live screenshot, then a vision-model escalation. TrainingDataGenerator.swift turns recorded (screenshot, accessibility state, click) tuples into JSONL grounding examples, and LoRATrainer.swift fine-tunes ShowUI-2B on them through the mlx-vlm Python package once enough new tuples accumulate. The README describes the capture of fourteen signal types, on-device Qwen and Whisper models, a 26-tool agent runtime, and points to a separate computer-use engine from the same publisher for full computer use. Cloud model features are optional with the user's own API key.

details.availability: Public Swift and Rust source built locally; models such as ShowUI-2B, Qwen and Whisper are downloaded separately during setup and are not covered by the repository license.

name: agent-computer-use
summary: Rust CLI (agent-cu) that lets agents snapshot desktop app accessibility trees into element refs or selectors and click, type, scroll or drag through AX on macOS, UI Automation on Windows and AT-SPI2 on Linux.
notes: Published on npm as agent-cu (package.json 0.1.1 at the inspected commit) with precompiled binaries, and also installable as an agent skill (skills/agent-computer-use/SKILL.md). Commands snapshot an app's accessibility tree into @eN refs or query it with a selector DSL (role, name, id, parent-child chains), then click, type, press keys, scroll, drag, move or resize windows, wait for elements, take screenshots, and run JSON batches or YAML workflows; output is JSON by default. Backends: macOS uses AXUIElement with CGEvent input, Windows uses UI Automation, and Linux uses AT-SPI2 over D-Bus with xdotool for input. Electron apps can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, but automatic Electron detection and relaunch with a debug port is implemented only on macOS (cli/crates/agent-computer-use-cdp/src/detect.rs). The README marks every platform as preview and states that the project is no longer maintained, recommending Cua Driver instead. The repository was formerly named kortix-ai/agent-click (same GitHub repository ID). The tool contains no model or agent loop.

Its default Ultrafast engine, adapted in TypeScript from browser-use/jev-ultrafast, launches Playwright Chromium, injects snapshot.js to list up to 250 visible interactive elements with roles and labels plus visible page text, has a decision model choose one click, fill, select, scroll or wait step at a time, and dispatches mouse and key events over the DevTools protocol (browser.ts); per server.mjs, screenshots serve recording and the inspector, with model input drawn from the page listing. config.mjs points decision requests at the hosted TypeSafe API (model jev-latest) by default and, unless overridden, generates typed text with the user's main model. name: AI Mime
summary: macOS app that records a demonstrated task, has an agent compile it into a portable skill of scripts, browser CDP steps and computer-use fallbacks, and patches the skill when a rerun breaks.
notes: Requires macOS 13 or newer, Python 3.12 and Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring permissions; Windows support remains pending. The recorder (pynput listeners and mss screenshots) writes a manifest of clicks, typing, hotkeys and scrolls with pre-action screenshots, plus optional extract and detail notes. Reflection turns the trace into a coordinate-free schema.json; an optimizer writes optimized_plan.json, preferring script steps, then browser_harness steps (Chrome CDP through a browser-harness git submodule), then ui_agent steps; a build agent packages a Claude Skill-compatible folder with run.sh, inputs and a fallback plan. The ui_agent drives the Mac in the foreground through cua-computer-server MCP tools, which AI Mime extends with combined screenshot-plus-accessibility-tree reads, and is told to target accessibility elements before screenshot coordinates. Agent runtimes are Anthropic (Claude Code) or OpenAI (Codex), selected during onboarding, with custom providers in user_config.yml. A prebuilt macOS DMG is linked from the README.

name: Gemini Browser Agent
summary: Chrome extension and Python WebSocket bridge that run Gemini 2.5 Computer Use on the user's active tab, sending tab screenshots to the model and executing its clicks, typing and scrolling via content scripts.
notes: The README calls the project a research experiment and scaffolding. websocket_agent.py is a local WebSocket server that calls gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025 through google-genai with the browser computer-use environment; widget/ is an unpacked Manifest V3 extension with a side panel where the user connects to the bridge and enters a goal. Each turn the extension captures the visible tab with chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab, the bridge converts the model's 0-1000 normalized coordinates to viewport pixels, and the extension carries out clicks, typing, key presses, hovering, scrolling and navigation by injecting functions (chrome.scripting.executeScript) that dispatch synthetic DOM events at document.elementFromPoint. Drag and drop is approximated with mousedown and mouseup events, unhandled model actions return an unimplemented warning, and the side panel sets a step limit (default 10). It needs a Gemini API key and acts in the user's own browser without a sandbox; the README points to the author's separate gemini-computer-use repository for sandboxed runs. The repository has no license file at the inspected commit.
